subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollout guardrails
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollout guardrails

Hi Alex and Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call so we’re all aligned on pain, goals, and next steps. I’ve attached a short PDF with highlights (discovery-recap.pdf) and an initial requirements sheet (observability-requirements.xlsx).

Pain points you shared
- Limited visibility into model-level regressions after rollouts (hard to attribute cause).
- No standardized golden prompt set or eval harness to catch quality drift.
- Current infra has ad-hoc tracing (no consistent hooks into generation calls), which makes debugging downstream failures slow.
- Dashboards are fragmented — engineering and product need separate views for latency/cost vs quality/regression.

Success criteria (what would make this a success in 30–60 days)
1) Dashboard(s) that show per-model/per-route latency, p50/p95/p99, and cost/token alongside quality metrics for a set of golden prompts.
2) Tracing hooks that correlate user requests -> model variant -> kernel/quantization profile for root-cause analysis.
3) Eval pipeline that runs golden prompt sets on new model rollouts and surfaces regression alerts (configurable thresholds + regression severity).
4) Rollout guardrails: automatic fallback to previous model variant or alternate region on regression detection, and a clear canary metric set.

What Redwood can provide (initial scope)
- Out-of-the-box dashboards (console) and a shared Drive folder with example dashboards and widgets.
- Tracing SDK: lightweight hooks you can add to your request flow (we’ll help instrument the first two endpoints).
- Eval harness + golden prompt set template, plus regression alerting tied into Slack/email and the Console.
- Rollout policy templates (canary windows, rollback thresholds, cross-region fallback).

Open questions / items we need from you
- Can you share a sample of 20–30 golden prompts you care most about? (we can redact PII)
- Who will own the instrumentation work on your side (engineer + approximate ETA)?
- Any compliance constraints around logs/trace retention we should be aware of?

Next steps
1) We’ll upload the initial dashboard templates and an eval harness example to the shared Drive by Mon, Aug 2. (link in this thread).
2) Dylan will coordinate a 60-minute tech session to walk through tracing hooks and identify the first two endpoints to instrument — proposed Wed, Aug 4.
3) Alex / Maya to send golden prompt list and confirm the eng owner by EOD Thu, Jul 30.

Attachments: discovery-recap.pdf, observability-requirements.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.s@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollout guardrails

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap and the attachments. This matches what we discussed. A few quick clarifications:

- We’ll put together the golden prompt list (20–30) by EOD Thu, Jul 30. Maya will own that.
- Instrumentation owner: that will be Priya (engineering lead). She’s cc’d internally but not on this thread; I’ll loop her in next after I sync with procurement on SSO/access.
- Compliance: we need traces retained for 90 days, with redaction for PHI fields — I’ll send the specific redaction rules.

Requests from our side
- Can you include an example of rollback thresholds you recommend for canaries? (short doc or bullets)
- We’d like the eval harness to support running against both current production model and a quantized variant (to check quality impact).

I’ve attached a draft SOW (SOW-draft.docx) for initial scope — procurement will review and come back with redlines.

Thanks — excited to move forward.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of AI Products | Acme Health
alex.j@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollout guardrails

Alex — thanks. Quick follow-up items from our side:

- I attached an initial set of recommended rollback thresholds and canary metric examples in the discovery-recap.pdf (see page 3). TL;DR: fail on >5% degradation in golden prompt pass-rate OR >20% increase in p95 latency during canary window.
- The eval harness supports running against multiple model variants out of the box — we’ll include a short guide on how to add a quantized variant to the job config in the Drive folder.
- Drive + HubSpot links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example and https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/9876543. We’ll also add the initial eval run to https://app.redwood.com/evals/ACME-OBS-001.

Next steps (confirmed)
- Alex / Maya: golden prompts + eng owner by EOD Thu, Jul 30.
- Dylan: calendar invite for Wed, Aug 4 11:00 AM PDT and Drive assets uploaded by Mon, Aug 2.
- Marissa + Logan: prep draft SOW notes for procurement review (we’ll review the SOW-draft.docx you attached).

If procurement needs any additional compliance evidence (SOC2, data retention, redaction capabilities), loop Logan and I and we’ll expedite.

Best,
Marissa
